title: Concession and nuanced clause relations
objectives: Select a connector for concession or contrast.
Form clauses after although and phrases after despite.
Distinguish established facts from hypothetical conditions.

explanation.heading: Meaning and use
paragraphs: Concession acknowledges a fact or possibility that might be expected to weaken another statement, while presenting the other statement as still valid. “Although the route was long, we arrived on time” accepts the length of the route but reports an outcome that may seem surprising. The two ideas are not logically incompatible; the writer presents their relationship as noteworthy.

A concessive expression can show that a writer has considered a counterpoint. “The sample is small. Nevertheless, the pattern merits investigation” acknowledges a limitation while maintaining a cautious conclusion. A concession is not evidence that the conclusion is true; it helps organise the argument.

explanation.heading: Form
paragraphs: Although and even though introduce clauses with a subject and finite verb: “Although the sample was small, the results were consistent.” Even though often makes the acknowledged contrast more emphatic. Despite and in spite of are prepositions and normally take a noun phrase or -ing clause: “Despite the small sample” or “Despite being tired”.

Nevertheless and nonetheless are linking adverbs, not subordinating conjunctions. They can introduce a separate sentence or follow a semicolon: “The sample was small. Nevertheless, the results were consistent.” “The sample was small; nevertheless, the results were consistent.” Punctuation conventions vary, but two independent clauses should not normally be joined by only a comma in standard edited prose.

explanation.heading: Examples in context
paragraphs: While can mark contrast rather than time: “The first method is inexpensive, while the second is faster.” Context determines the intended relation. Whereas often marks a contrast between two features: “The north was dry, whereas the south was wet.” Neither connector by itself says that one clause causes the other.

“Even if the results improve, the team will continue testing” considers a possible condition and says the action will hold regardless. “Even though the results improved, the team continued testing” treats improvement as an established fact in the stated past context. Preserve that difference when rewriting.

explanation.heading: Contrasts and common mistakes
paragraphs: Avoid following despite directly with a finite clause: use “Despite the delay” or “Despite the fact that there was a delay”, not “Despite there was a delay”. With although, use a finite clause: “Although there was a delay”. “Despite the fact that” is grammatical but can be wordier than a simple although-clause.

Do not insert but after although in the same basic two-clause construction: “Although it rained, we left”, not “Although it rained, but we left”. In other contexts a later but may introduce an additional contrast. Select the connector and punctuation to show the actual relationship between the ideas.

examples.sentence: Although the route was long, we arrived on time.
examples.note: Although introduces a finite concessive clause.

examples.sentence: Despite the delay, the meeting started on time.
examples.note: Despite takes the noun phrase the delay.

examples.sentence: Despite being tired, she completed the report.
The sample was small; nevertheless, the results were consistent.
The north was dry, whereas the south was wet.
examples.note: Whereas presents a contrast between conditions.

examples.sentence: Even if it rains, we will go.
examples.note: Even if presents a possible condition.

examples.sentence: Even though it rained, we went.
examples.note: Even though presents rain as an established past fact here.

examples.sentence: While the first route is shorter, the second is safer.
examples.note: While expresses contrast in this context.

common_errors.incorrect: Despite there was a delay, we arrived on time.
common_errors.correct: Despite the delay, we arrived on time.
common_errors.reason: Despite takes a noun phrase here, not a bare finite clause.

common_errors.incorrect: Although it rained, but we left.
common_errors.reason: Do not add but to the basic although construction.

common_errors.incorrect: Despite she was tired, she finished.
common_errors.correct: Although she was tired, she finished.
common_errors.reason: Although introduces the finite clause she was tired.

summary: Concession acknowledges a point while maintaining another claim.
Although takes a finite clause; despite takes a noun phrase or -ing clause.
Distinguish an established fact with even though from a possible condition with even if.

exercises.prompt: Choose a concessive finite clause.
exercises.explanation: Although introduces the finite clause the route was long.

options.text: Despite the delay, we left.
Despite being tired, she worked.
Although the route was long, we arrived on time.
The sample was small; nevertheless, it was useful.

option_feedback.a: “Despite the delay, we left.” does not fit here. Although introduces the finite clause the route was long.
option_feedback.b: “Despite being tired, she worked.” does not fit here. Although introduces the finite clause the route was long.
option_feedback.c: “Although the route was long, we arrived on time.” fits here. Although introduces the finite clause the route was long.
option_feedback.d: “The sample was small; nevertheless, it was useful.” does not fit here. Although introduces the finite clause the route was long.
